justification: One condition in the production extract child: the address-space cap is no longer applied when the AI reader runs. Without this the nightly extract reads no pages and never finishes, so no changed chapter gets new rules.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured 2026-10-26: Railway dcp-extract logged '[extractor] LLM document reader (sol)' and then no '[reader]' line for over two hours, at DCP_PDF_MEM_LIMIT 2 GB and again at 4 GB. Locally in Linux the same Sol call on chunk 1 returned in 75 s uncapped and hung forever under a 2 GB RLIMIT_AS.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The cap was sized for the regex reader's PDF parsing peaks of 127 to 726 MB; it was never measured against the AI reader's network client, which stalls under it.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: The regex reader keeps the cap exactly as before. The AI reader runs uncapped and stays bounded by the existing wall-clock budget and the child process isolation.
pre_impl.external_source_error: No new external call; the same Sol request now gets an answer.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: every changed chapter waiting for the AI reader never got new rules and the batch hung until its time budget ran out. After: the chapters are read; a runaway AI child is still killed by the time budget.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: the cap is set for the AI reader, or no longer set for the regex reader
falsifiable_check.observed_red: YES: reverting the condition to 'if mem_limit_bytes:' fails test_the_memory_ceiling_is_set_for_the_regex_reader_but_never_the_ai_reader under Linux; restored, 7 pass.

functions.name: _pdf_work_child
functions.input: queue, pdf path, chapter config, ai_on flag and the memory cap in bytes
functions.output: one result dict on the queue; the cap is applied only when ai_on is false
functions.if_none: a zero or missing cap applies no limit, the same as before this change

break_it.scenario: AI reader chapter on Railway with the 4 GB cap
break_it.what_happens: no cap is set, so the Sol call returns and pages are read

break_it.scenario: Regex reader chapter with a pathological PDF
break_it.what_happens: the cap is still set and a runaway child is killed before the host
break_it.how: ai_on false keeps the old path

break_it.scenario: AI child that genuinely runs away on memory
break_it.what_happens: the parent's wall-clock budget kills it and the batch moves to the next chapter; a host OOM kill is contained by the child process
break_it.how: existing extract_pdf_isolated timeout and process isolation
